newsitem.title: UK: Guinness Flight starts global privatisation index.
newsitem.headline: Guinness Flight starts global privatisation index.

text.p: British fund management group Guinness Flight on Friday launched an index to track performance of the top 200 international privatisation stocks.

It said it had launched the GFP200 index amid frustration about the lack of an appropriate benchmark for its privatisation funds -- a 50 million sterling unit trust and a 75 million sterling Guernsey-domiciled offshore fund.

"The special features of privatisation stocks and the significance of the retail investor in privatisation issues warrant a special index to accurately determine their short and long term track record," Guinness Flight said.

It said the universe of privatisation stocks showed some systematic outperformance against the world benchmark indices, returning a total 145.4 percent in the 78 month period starting on January 1, 1991. The MSCI World (ex-US) index returned 88.6 percent in total over the period.
The index is calculated using the estimated free-float market capitalisation of each of the index constituents.
The UK is the top country in the index with a 27 percent weighting, with France second at 11 percent followed by Brazil, Italy, Germany and others.
Utilities companies represent 44 percent of the index, followed by natural resources with 24 percent and financials at 15 percent.
The market capitalisation of the index at end-June was $833 billion.
